evidence.where: Header row of each Morticd10 data file (Deaths1 is all ages)

evidence.quote: Access the WHO interactive mortality database
evidence.where: WHO Mortality Database page, link beside the raw-data downloads (Morticd10 parts 1 to 6, country codes, documentation)

tried: platform.who.int/mortality is an interactive portal; WHO's own raw ICD-10 files on cdn.who.int were used instead, unzipped and filtered in the browser (nothing saved to disk). Rows with Admin1 or SubDiv set (sub-national) were excluded; sexes 1, 2 and 9 were included.
2024 is in the files but only 37 countries have reported it (X71 1,087; Y21 835), so it is noted rather than recorded; 2023 is the most recent year with broad reporting (69 countries).
Check against another source: the files give the United States 4,337 W65-W74 deaths for 2021, consistent with the MMWR's 4,677 for W65-W74 plus V90 and V92 that year.
notes: Most recent year with broad reporting is 2023: X71 3,394 and Y21 3,407 deaths across 69 countries reporting a detailed ICD-10 list. For context, 2022 (88 countries): X71 3,638, Y21 3,796; 2019, the broadest recent year (106 countries): X71 3,963, Y21 4,290. In 2023, 11 of the 69 countries recorded no X71 or Y21 death. The same countries recorded 34,732 unintentional drowning deaths (W65-W74) in 2023, so in the reporting countries intentional and undetermined drownings together are of the order of one fifth of the unintentional count; that ratio is the reviewer's to state, not recorded as a row. Totals are the lab's sums over one database's national rows, labelled as such on every row.
